note: The Law on the Credit Bureau (Закон за кредитно биро), consolidated text covering Official Gazette 81/08, 24/11, 199/14, 192/15 and 83/18, in the Macedonian Credit Bureau's own copy on mkb.mk (a scan of a Word document, read by eye on 2026-10-31). Article 19: the credit bureau keeps the data it receives for five years after the obligation is repaid or the subject's account is closed. The law counts only from repayment or closure, so a late payment stays while unpaid: written as keep 30, the longest the game keeps (the convention for 'kept as long as unpaid'), lifting five years after it is paid, 1826 days (five years of 365.25 days). The later amending law (Official Gazette 122/2021, read from archive.org's snapshot of 17 September 2021 of the bureau's copy) changes only the country's name and the fines, not Article 19; no later amendment was looked for beyond the bureau's own documents page. Article 6(3): data reach the bureau at the frequency set in each provider's contract with it, so no source states how many days after its due date a missed payment is reported: the days are the game's reading, the next monthly update. The bureau's name is from its own 'About' page (archive.org snapshot of 26 August 2018). The National Bank's separate Credit Register is not this file's subject.

sources.title: Македонско кредитно биро: Закон за кредитно биро, пречистен текст (Сл. весник 81/08, 24/11, 199/14, 192/15 и 83/18), scan (read by eye)
sources.said: Кредитното биро е должно да ги чува добиените податоци во период од пет години по исплатата на обврската или затворањето на сметката на субјектот на податоците. ... Податоците од ставот (1) на овој член се доставуваат до кредитното биро во динамика утврдена со договорот склучен меѓу кредитното биро и давателот на податоци.
